messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'mistral-vpc' reporting sustained GPU utilization at 99% for tenant 'OrchidLabs'. Queue length growing, token generation queuing. Severity: P1. Paging on-call.

jess_oncall: oncall here, ack. who is seeing customer impact? :eyes:

maya_sre: seeing tail latency spikes + request queueing on mistral-vpc tasks. grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abcd. Error rate up ~12% over 5m.

sam_eng: OrchidLabs support flagged 503s from their inference endpoints. They say production traffic is affected.

alex_prod: note — this is a single-tenant dedicated VPC pool for OrchidLabs. No automatic shared burst configured. Options: emergency burst to shared pool, manual scale-up, or throttle customer traffic.

jess_oncall: quick options summary: (A) emergency burst (attach 2 GPUs from shared) — infra approval needed; (B) trigger manual scale up (provisioning time ~6-10m); (C) apply rate limiting on Orchid routes to reduce errors now. Any objections to trying C + B concurrently?

emily_cs: FYI Orchid is high-touch prod. They prefer scale up > throttling, but tolerable if we warn. I'll hold communications.

maya_sre: I'll kick the scale job now: `./tools/scale_pools --pool mistral-vpc --add-gpus 2 --reason "emergency orchid burst"`

ops-bot: infra check: shared pool has 4 available GPUs in region-us-west. Emergency attach requires infra-lead approval (@raj_infra).

alex_prod: pinging @raj_infra for approval to allocate 2 GPUs to mistral-vpc for ~30m. Customer impact ongoing.

raj_infra: ack. We can spare 2 GPUs for emergency allocation. Approving immediate attach. Will cordon and attach — ~7min to be ready.

maya_sre: running scale now, logs:
```
> PATCH /api/pools/mistral-vpc/scale
status: 202 Accepted
instance_provision: queued
estimated_ready: ~6m
```

maya_sre: also enabling a soft rate-limit on Orchid routes to reduce bursty requests while scaling: `routes.orchid.rate_limit = 0.75` + fallback 429. Will keep it conservative.

jess_oncall: good. Emily, notify Orchid with a short note: "We're applying temporary scaling and a short rate-limit to reduce errors; will update when stable." Keep it non-technical.

emily_cs: message sent to customer. They replied: "Prefer scale up over throttling — please escalate." I forwarded.

sam_eng: if attach takes >5m, recommend adding a short-lived token-bucket limiter on the most expensive endpoints as well. I can patch route rules.

maya_sre: attach completed:
```
> /api/pools/attach
status: success
attached_gpus: 2
pool_total_gpus: 10 -> 12
ready_nodes: 2
```

maya_sre: metrics: queue length dropping, tail latency back toward baseline within ~90s. Monitoring for 5m to confirm.

jess_oncall: great. Let's keep this emergency allocation for 30m, then scale down once queue drained. Also raise follow-up ticket to investigate autoscaler thresholds & traffic patterns for Orchid.

alex_prod: action items: (1) postmortem on autoscaler config, (2) consider reserved burst for enterprise VPCs, (3) update runbook to include emergency attach steps.

emily_cs: Orchid confirms errors reduced and thanks the team. They asked for a post-incident summary.

maya_sre: scheduling scale-down in 30m. Running final health checks.

ops-bot: scheduled scale-down at 1732106800 (UTC).

jess_oncall: assigning follow-up ticket INC-1732105000 to maya_sre for root cause & remediation. Marking incident resolved-active-mitigations. :white_check_mark:

end of thread.
